strategy.summary: CART-12 prices the cart at checkout via cartTotal(items, { coupon }) in src/cart.js: 10% bulk discount at 10+ items (summed quantities), SAVE5 coupon applied after the bulk discount with goods floored at $0, unknown coupons refused, and $4.99 shipping unless discounted goods are $50+ (empty cart is free). Unit tests in Vitest must prove each rule and its boundaries through cartTotal's returned total. Reading the code: bulkDiscount uses `itemCount > BULK_THRESHOLD`, so a cart of exactly 10 items gets no discount, contradicting AC1 and the constant's own doc comment ("at least this many"); that case is planned as an expected failure with a defect report.
inScope: cartTotal, bulkDiscount behaviour as seen in cartTotal's result
Bulk-discount threshold boundaries (9, 10, 11 items across several lines)
SAVE5 ordering after the bulk discount and the $0 floor on goods
Free-shipping threshold boundaries based on discounted goods, empty cart
outOfScope: UI or API for checkout (none exists in the repo)
Other coupon codes beyond SAVE5 (ticket defines only SAVE5)
assumptions: cartTotal(items, { coupon }) is the checkout pricing entry point; items are { price, quantity }.
Totals are rounded to cents by the code, so exact toBe comparisons on dollar amounts are used.
Coupon codes are case-sensitive (only 'SAVE5' exists in the code); 'save5' is treated as another code and refused.
A refused coupon is signalled by cartTotal throwing an Error whose message names the submitted code.
openQuestions: Should the coupon be accepted case-insensitively (e.g. 'save5')? The code refuses it; tests follow the code.
With SAVE5 on a cart under $5, goods become $0 but shipping $4.99 still applies (the code's behaviour; ticket only says goods never cost less than $0).

risks.description: Off-by-one on the bulk threshold (exactly 10 items not discounted)
risks.mitigation: TC1 exercises exactly 10 items across two lines (expected failure, defect recorded); TC2/TC3 pin 11 and 9 items with normal passing tests.

risks.description: Coupon applied before the bulk discount, or goods going negative
risks.mitigation: TC4 chooses amounts where the order changes the total; TC5 uses a cart cheaper than the coupon.

risks.description: Free shipping computed on the pre-discount subtotal or with > instead of >=
risks.mitigation: TC7 exact $50, TC8 subtotal above $50 but discounted goods below, TC9 just below $50.

acceptanceCriteria.text: A cart with 10 or more items in total (sum of line quantities) gets 10% off its subtotal; fewer than 10 items get no bulk discount.
Coupon SAVE5 takes $5 off after the bulk discount and the goods never cost less than $0; any other coupon code is refused with an error.
Shipping is free when the goods cost $50 or more after discounts, otherwise $4.99; an empty cart costs nothing.

testCases.expected: Total 54 (60 less 10%, free shipping). Code currently returns 60 (uses > instead of >=): marked it.fails and recorded as a defect.
testCases.rationale: Boundary of AC1; the code's > comparison misses it.

testCases.expected: Total 51.99 (47 + 4.99); a subtotal-based check would give 47

charges nothing for an empty cart

defects.title: Cart of exactly 10 items gets no bulk discount
defects.description: AC1: a cart with 10 or more items in total gets 10% off. bulkDiscount in src/cart.js:22 checks itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD (10), so exactly 10 items get no discount. This also contradicts the comment on BULK_THRESHOLD ("at least this many"). Expected cartTotal of 4×$6 + 6×$6 = 54; actual 60.
defects.evidence: TC1 is marked it.fails and passes in run 0 (so the assertion toBe(54) fails); src/cart.js:22 `itemCount(items) > BULK_THRESHOLD`.
